instructions.name: absorb_loss
docs: Use protocol buffer for loss absorption

instructions.name: add_yield_to_buffer
docs: Add yield to the global protocol buffer (from yield harvesting)

instructions.name: admin_fund
docs: Admin deposits USDC into the global vault to seed markets.
Replaces the prior user-facing `global_deposit`. No shares are minted — the
protocol is the sole LP, capital is operator-funded.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Admin authority — must match `global_clp.authority`.

accounts.name: admin_collateral
docs: Admin's USDC source account.

accounts.name: global_vault
docs: Global USDC vault: ATA(global_clp_pda, usdc_mint)

instructions.name: admin_withdraw
docs: Admin withdraws idle cUSDC from the global vault to the treasury
destination, rate-limited by the `TreasuryPolicy` token bucket.
Only idle balance can be pulled — capital already allocated to markets
must first be recalled via `return_to_global`. Blocked while frozen.
The allowance accrues at `rate_per_sec` up to `burst`; a withdrawal may
not exceed it, and spends it. The destination is fixed by the policy.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Admin authority — must match `global_clp.authority`.

accounts.name: global_vault
docs: Global cUSDC vault, owned by the GlobalClp PDA.

accounts.name: destination
docs: The policy's destination; nothing else can receive a withdrawal.

instructions.name: advance_to_market
docs: Lend treasury cUSDC to a market's collateral vault for LIQUIDITY only
(r58 lever 3): mint-redeem's `receive_advance`, with the GlobalClp PDA
as the funder. Unlike `backstop_market` (one-way, unchanged) this is a
reversible loan: it is NOT credited to the market's `total_collateral`,
it is capped per market by `MarketAdvance.max_advance_bps`, and
mint-redeem's `repay_advance` returns it to the global vault when the
market's own recall lands. The signer must be global_clp.authority AND
market.authority. Refused while the guardian has the treasury frozen.
Not charged to the withdrawal allowance: the cash stays protocol-owned
until a settle pays a redeemer what the market owes them.

accounts.name: authority
docs: global_clp.authority, which must also be market.authority.

instructions.name: allocate_to_market
docs: Transfer USDC from the global vault to a per-market operating vault (keeper).
Refused while the guardian has the treasury frozen (AUDIT CLP-3); the
reverse move, `return_to_global`, is never blocked.

accounts.name: global_vault
docs: Global USDC vault: must be owned by the GlobalClp PDA.

accounts.name: clp_vault
docs: Per-market operating vault: owned by this market's Clp PDA and of the
global vault's mint.

instructions.name: apply_treasury_limits
docs: Apply the pending treasury change once its delay has passed.
Permissionless: any signer may crank it.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone: applying a change that has waited out its delay is a crank.

instructions.name: backstop_market
docs: Move treasury cUSDC from the global vault straight into a market's
collateral, crediting its `total_collateral`, via mint-redeem's
`fund_collateral_from` with the GlobalClp PDA as the funder. The signer
must be global_clp.authority AND market.authority (mint-redeem's
`has_one`). Not rate-limited: the funds stay protocol-owned, landing in
the market's own collateral vault. Refused while the guardian has the
treasury frozen (AUDIT CLP-3): from there mint-redeem can deploy them.

accounts.name: authority
docs: global_clp.authority, which must also be market.authority.

accounts.name: treasury_policy
docs: Read for `frozen` (AUDIT CLP-3). Appended last so every earlier account
keeps its position.

instructions.name: cancel_swap
docs: Refund an expired order to its owner, escrow and rent included. Allowed
STRICTLY after `expires_at` (settle owns <=, cancel owns >: no gap, no
overlap). Permissionless since 11 Oct 2026: the order is already dead and
every token goes to its owner, so a crank (the keeper) may send it.
Deliberately checks NOTHING else, no frozen/enabled/oracle/is_active:
escrowed funds are always recoverable after the TTL regardless of
protocol state. A new order refunds only to its recorded `user_in`; a
legacy order to any account of its owner for the escrow's mint. When that
account cannot receive, the escrow is kept and the order becomes
ORDER_CLAIMABLE for `claim` (AUDIT CLP-5: refunds cannot be blocked).

accounts.name: user
docs: The order's owner: receives the refund and all rent. It need not sign:
the handler only acts on an EXPIRED order and pays only the owner, so
anyone (the keeper, as a crank) can clear a dead order.

accounts.name: escrow
docs: The order's escrow; its PDA (stored bump) is checked in the handler.

accounts.name: user_in
docs: the owner for the escrow mint for a legacy one. If it cannot receive, the
escrow is held for `claim`.

instructions.name: cancel_treasury_limits
docs: Drop the pending treasury change (global_clp.authority or guardian).

instructions.name: check_inventory_restrictions
docs: Check if operations should be restricted based on inventory state

instructions.name: claim
docs: Release what a settle or cancel held for an order whose recorded account
could not receive (closed, re-owned, frozen or wrong mint). Permissionless,
like `cancel_swap`: every token goes to accounts owned by `order.user`,
the escrow and order rent to `order.user`, and the claim account's rent
back to the keeper that paid it. A trading-account order (owned by the
trader PDA) is claimed by a crank because that PDA cannot sign here.

accounts.name: claim_payer
docs: rent back); ignored otherwise.

accounts.name: refund_to
docs: `order.user` for the escrow's mint when the escrow holds any.

accounts.name: payout_to
docs: `order.user` for the claim's mint when it holds any.

instructions.name: clp_burn_excess
docs: Burn ASYMMETRIC excess L or S inventory held by the CLP PDA without
receiving collateral. Used to retire zombie-pool recoveries — when
`drain-zombie-positions` lands tokens in CLP's L/S ATAs that would
otherwise sit there forever (since paired-redeem requires equal
L+S quantities and asymmetric residue can't be paired-redeemed).
SAFETY (mirrors keeper_burn_single's hardening):
- Admin-gated via `has_one = authority` on Clp.
- The CPI'd `permissionless_burn` ix has its own L/S mint
address-binding, so even if the wrong mints were passed at
this layer the inner ix would reject them.
- No cUSDC transfer in either layer.

accounts.name: market
docs: mint-redeem Market PDA — supply field gets decremented via CPI.
Bind to clp.market_id so a different market's `Market` can't be
substituted to corrupt cross-market `total_l/s_supply` ledgers.

accounts.name: clp_long_account
docs: CLP's long token ATA. Owner must be the CLP PDA, mint pinned to
the market's long_mint (see comment on ClpBurnExcess).

accounts.name: clp_short_account
docs: CLP's short token ATA — same shape as clp_long_account.

instructions.name: clp_fund_pool_synth
docs: Move synth from the CLP's L/S ATA into a pool's ask vault (the refill leg
after `vault_mint_pairs`). The inventory was already counted as deployed at
mint time (`vault_l/s_deployed`), so no counters change — this just stages
it into the pool book for the next `set_pool_shape`. Keeper/admin-gated via
`has_one = authority` on Clp; the CLP PDA signs the outbound transfer.

accounts.name: pool
docs: Pool whose ask vault receives the synth (market binding checked in handler).

accounts.name: clp_synth_account
docs: CLP-owned synth ATA, source (owner/mint validated in handler).

accounts.name: pool_synth_vault
docs: Pool-owned synth vault, destination (owner/mint validated in handler).

instructions.name: clp_fund_pool_usdc
docs: Move cUSDC from the market's CLP vault into a pool's bid vault: the
bid-side refill. Sell flow spends a book's bid cUSDC and turns it into
synth; `pool_sweep_synth` returns the synth, and this puts the cUSDC
back. Keeper/admin-gated via `has_one = authority` on Clp; the CLP PDA
signs the outbound transfer.

accounts.name: pool
docs: Pool whose bid vault receives the cUSDC (market binding checked in handler).

accounts.name: clp_vault
docs: CLP-owned per-market cUSDC vault, source (owner/mint validated in handler).

accounts.name: pool_usdc_vault
docs: Pool-owned cUSDC vault, destination (owner/mint validated in handler).

instructions.name: clp_swap
docs: Retired 11 Oct 2026. The v2 oracle-pegged instant swap filled at the
last pushed NAV, a stale quote between pushes, and nothing could hold it
to the hours when that price is fresh. Trades now go through committed
orders (`commit_swap` / `settle_swap`, filled at the next push) while a
market is open, and the bin books or the Manifest order book while it is
closed. The accounts are kept so existing clients still decode; every
call fails with `SwapDisabled`.

accounts.name: user_usdc
docs: User's cUSDC token account.

accounts.name: user_synth
docs: User's synth token account for the chosen side (mint validated in handler).

accounts.name: clp
docs: Per-market CLP PDA — seeds bind it to `market`.

accounts.name: clp_vault
docs: CLP's cUSDC operating vault (owner == clp PDA, validated in handler).

accounts.name: clp_synth
docs: CLP's synth inventory for the chosen side (owner == clp PDA, mint validated).

accounts.name: market
docs: The mint-redeem Market PDA — source of NAV + solvency fields (read-only).

instructions.name: collect_fees
docs: Collect trading fees (called by protocol)

instructions.name: commit_swap
docs: Escrow `amount_in` (cUSDC for buys / synth for sells) into an Order-owned
token account. The keeper settles it via `settle_swap` at the next oracle
push; `cancel_swap` refunds after the TTL. The payout (`user_out`) and
source (`user_in`) accounts are recorded in the Order: settle and cancel
pay only there, or hold the tokens for `claim` (AUDIT CLP-5).

accounts.name: user
docs: Pays rent for the order + escrow (both refunded on any terminal path).

accounts.name: market
docs: The mint-redeem Market PDA (read-only; binds side mints).

accounts.name: clp
docs: Per-market CLP PDA (read-only here; fail-fast guard checks).

accounts.name: in_mint
docs: Mint of the escrowed (input) leg — validated against side/direction in the handler.

accounts.name: escrow
docs: Escrow for the committed funds, owned by the order PDA.

accounts.name: user_in
docs: User's source token account (owner/mint validated in handler).

accounts.name: user_out
docs: User's PAYOUT token account — must exist at commit so settlement can't
strand the order on a missing ATA (owner/mint validated in handler).

accounts.name: clp_vault
docs: CLP's cUSDC vault — read-only anchor for the cUSDC mint (owner checked in handler).

instructions.name: configure_inventory_budget
docs: Configure inventory budget thresholds (admin only)

instructions.name: configure_liquidity_seeder
docs: Configure the liquidity seeder threshold on the global vault (admin only).

instructions.name: configure_pool_geom
docs: Configure the 2-zone bin geometry (r30/r31): fine `core_bins` near NAV at the
pool's `step_bps`, then `wing_step_bps` for the outer wings (the float band).
`wing_step_bps == 0` resets to the uniform ladder. Validated: wing ≥ core and
core_bins ≤ num_bins.

instructions.name: configure_revenue_attribution
docs: Update the registered keeper authorities (admin only). Counters and
`started_at` are untouched — this only re-points the classifier (e.g.
keeper key rotation, temporary test keypairs).

instructions.name: configure_swap
docs: Configure the v2 native oracle-pegged swap guards (admin only). Each
`None` arg leaves that field unchanged. `enabled=true` turns the native
swap path on; `frozen=true` is the hard kill switch.

instructions.name: configure_yield_strategy
docs: Configure yield strategy (admin only)

instructions.name: deposit_profit
docs: Deposit arb or spread profit from keeper.
Takes a TVL-based continuous flow tax to dev wallet; rest goes to global vault.

accounts.name: global_vault
docs: Global vault receives the CLP portion of profit. It must be the treasury's own
account: the profit counters below count only money that reached it.

accounts.name: revenue_attribution
docs: Appended LAST — keeps prior indices stable for the keeper's hand-built
account list.

instructions.name: freeze_treasury
docs: Freeze treasury withdrawals (global_clp.authority or guardian).

instructions.name: get_yield_status
docs: Get current yield deployment status, gated by live oracle market state.

instructions.name: init_pool
docs: Create the per-(market, side) pool. Admin-only (pinned to global_clp).

accounts.name: global_clp
docs: Pins pool creation to the global admin.

instructions.name: init_revenue_attribution
docs: One-time setup of the RevenueAttribution singleton (admin only). Must
run immediately after the program upgrade that added it — pool_swap
requires the PDA to exist. Counters start at zero; `started_at` = now.

accounts.name: global_clp
docs: Pins setup to the global admin.

instructions.name: init_treasury_policy
docs: One-time setup of the treasury withdrawal policy (global_clp.authority,
which also pays). Allowance starts at 0 and accrues from now.

accounts.name: authority
docs: global_clp.authority; pays for the policy account.

accounts.name: destination
docs: Must be `params.destination` and hold the global vault's mint.

instructions.name: init_treasury_yield
docs: Open the treasury's lending ledger (authority, once).

instructions.name: initialize_clp
docs: Initialize clp fund for a market

instructions.name: initialize_global_clp
docs: One-time setup: create the GlobalClp account and global USDC vault.

instructions.name: pool_swap
docs: Swap against the pool book. direction: 0 = buy synth (pay cUSDC), 1 = sell
synth (receive cUSDC). Walks the bins (real slippage), enforces `min_out`.
Remaining accounts when the market is capped (`oi_cap > 0`): the pool long
and short synth vaults, then the CLP's long and short token accounts
(mint_redeem::exposure::inventory_keys). A fill that would push traders'
net position past the cap reverts.

accounts.name: clp
docs: Per-market CLP — carries the swap_guards + rolling-window notional-cap
state (audit H3). Bound to the pool's market via seeds.

accounts.name: revenue_attribution
docs: Keeper-vs-external revenue split. Appended LAST so pre-existing account
indices stay stable for hand-built encoders.

accounts.name: market
docs: The pool's market, read for its price age: the book trades only while
the market floats. Appended after revenue_attribution for the same reason.

instructions.name: pool_sweep_synth
docs: Sweep excess SYNTH out of a pool's ask vault back into the CLP's synth ATA
(the reverse of the refill leg). Ask depth beyond ~the bid side's value is
pure arb bait (r36c: toxic loss scales with deployed depth, revenue is
demand-capped) and reads as fake exit capacity; trimmed synth returns to
CLP custody where it serves committed-order provisioning instead.
Keeper/admin-gated via `has_one = authority`; the pool PDA signs.

accounts.name: pool
docs: Pool whose ask vault is being trimmed (market binding checked in handler).

accounts.name: pool_synth_vault
docs: Pool-owned synth vault, source (owner/mint validated in handler).

accounts.name: clp_synth_account
docs: CLP-owned synth ATA, destination (owner/mint validated in handler).

instructions.name: pool_sweep_usdc
docs: Sweep accumulated cUSDC out of a pool's bid vault back into the per-market
CLP vault. One-directional buy flow converts a pool's ask inventory into
cUSDC that piles up in `usdc_vault`; the keeper sweeps it here so
`vault_mint_pairs` can recycle it into fresh L+S inventory (elastic refill).
Keeper/admin-gated via `has_one = authority` on Clp; the pool PDA signs the
outbound transfer.

accounts.name: pool
docs: Pool whose bid vault is being swept (market binding checked in handler).

accounts.name: pool_usdc_vault
docs: Pool-owned cUSDC vault (owner/mint validated in handler).

accounts.name: clp_vault
docs: CLP-owned per-market cUSDC vault (owner/mint validated in handler).

instructions.name: realloc_clp
docs: Realloc CLP account to fit new fields added after initial deployment.
Must be called once per CLP before any liquidity seeding instructions.

accounts.name: clp
docs: the old (pre-upgrade) account can be extended to the new size.

accounts.name: global_clp
docs: GlobalClp pins the trusted authority. We can't `has_one = authority`
against `clp` because it's `AccountInfo` (intentional — the old
schema may not deserialize), so we anchor authentication here.

instructions.name: realloc_pool
docs: Keeper reposition: set the active price (≈ NAV) and the per-bin shape.
Grow an existing Pool account to fit the 2-zone fields (wing_step_bps, core_bins)
added after initial deployment. RAW realloc on an UncheckedAccount — we do NOT
deserialize the new struct from the short account (that fails 3003); instead we
validate owner + the authority prefix (Pool.authority is bytes 8..40), fund the rent
delta, then grow with zero-fill (new fields → 0 → bin_geom() = uniform, backward compat).

accounts.name: pool
docs: deserialize the grown struct from a still-short account (that fails AccountDidNotDeserialize).

instructions.name: record_deployment
docs: Record a yield deployment (called after keeper deploys to protocol).
Reads market state directly from the oracle account to gate deployment limits.

accounts.name: oracle_config
docs: market_state (Active/Passive) is read at byte offset ORACLE_MARKET_STATE_OFFSET.

instructions.name: record_harvest
docs: Record yield harvest — updates per-market deployment and global protocol buffer.

instructions.name: record_withdrawal
docs: Record a yield withdrawal (called after keeper withdraws from protocol)

instructions.name: return_to_global
docs: Return USDC from a per-market vault back to the global vault (keeper).

accounts.name: global_vault
docs: Global USDC vault: must be owned by the GlobalClp PDA.

accounts.name: clp_vault
docs: Per-market operating vault: owned by this market's Clp PDA and of the
global vault's mint, so neither direction can pay a foreign account.

instructions.name: set_commit_spread
docs: Post the vol-scaled committed-order half-spread (bps). Keeper-driven from
the same vol model as the book; `settle_swap` floors it at COMMIT_SPREAD_BPS.
Authority-gated (clp.authority) like the other swap config. Cheap/frequent.

instructions.name: set_pool_shape
docs: `asks`/`bids` must each sum to ≤ the pool's synth/cUSDC vault balance.
This is also the rebalance-to-NAV (LVR capture by repricing the book).

accounts.name: synth_vault
docs: CLP-owned synth vault (owner == pool, validated in handler).

accounts.name: usdc_vault
docs: CLP-owned cUSDC vault (owner == pool, validated in handler).

instructions.name: set_treasury_guardian
docs: Rotate the guardian (current guardian only, immediate). A pending
change that kept the old guardian follows the rotation, so applying it
later cannot silently restore the key that was just rotated out.

instructions.name: set_treasury_limits
docs: Change the treasury limits (global_clp.authority). Accrues first. If
every field is equal or tighter (rate and burst not higher, delay not
shorter, destination and guardian unchanged) it applies at once, clamps
the allowance to the new burst and clears any pending change. Otherwise
all five fields become the pending change, applicable after the CURRENT
`delay_secs`; this overwrites any earlier pending change.

accounts.name: destination
docs: Must be `params.destination` and hold the global vault's mint.

instructions.name: settle_swap
docs: Keeper-only settlement (AUDIT CLP-5): the signer must be `clp.authority`
or `market.keeper_authority`, so the order owner cannot pick which push
fills. Fills the order at NAV(now) ± the committed spread, valid only when
`market.twap_updated_at` is STRICTLY newer than the commit (the
no-latency-arb property) and the oracle is healthy. min_out miss → full
refund (terminal), so orders can't revert-loop. Inventory shortfall →
revert (stays pending; the keeper provisions and retries).
No account the owner controls can make it fail. A new order pays only to
the accounts recorded at commit (`order.user_out`, `order.user_in`); a
legacy (pre-upgrade) order pays to the accounts passed, checked for owner
and mint. When the payout account cannot receive (closed, re-owned,
frozen, wrong mint) the output goes into the order's claim token account
`[b"claim", order]`, created here with the keeper's rent; when the refund
account cannot receive, the tokens stay in the escrow. Either way the
order stays open as ORDER_CLAIMABLE and `claim` releases it. Otherwise
all rent returns to the order's user, as before.
MAINNET PREREQUISITE (AUDIT C1 — BLOCKER, needs Pyth feed integration +
cutover decision): today the fill price and the freshness timestamp are
BOTH keeper-written (`user_twap_price` / `twap_updated_at`), so a
compromised/lagging keeper can post a favorable price and settle against
it with no independent anchor. Before any mainnet deploy, settlement must
read Pyth directly at this code point and enforce
`pyth.publish_time > order.created_at` (replacing `is_settle_fresh` on the
keeper timestamp) plus a confidence/staleness gate — keeping keeper-TWAP
only as an explicit governance-gated ProxyMode fallback. This is the same
freshness anchor `pool_swap` needs for its Normal-mode staleness freeze
(H3 added the rolling-window notional cap already; the freeze waits on
this). Sequence it behind a shadow-run of Pyth vs keeper-TWAP per market.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: The keeper. Writable: it pays the claim account's rent when the owner's
payout account cannot receive (refunded at `claim`).

accounts.name: escrow
docs: The order's escrow; its PDA (stored bump) is checked in the handler.

accounts.name: clp
docs: Per-market CLP PDA (mut: swap_prev_price advances on an accepted fill).

accounts.name: user_out
docs: of the owner for the payout mint for a legacy one). Paid only if it can
receive; otherwise the payout goes to `claim`.

accounts.name: user_in
docs: it can receive; otherwise the tokens stay in the escrow for `claim`.

accounts.name: claim
docs: (and its address checked) only when the payout account cannot receive.

accounts.name: out_mint
docs: the handler; needed to create the claim account.

instructions.name: sweep_clp_lamports
docs: Move the lamports a per-market `Clp` account holds above its rent-exempt
minimum to the authority (global_clp.authority, which must also be the
Clp's own authority). The excess on devnet is Meteora position rent that
was refunded to these PDAs. Only `Clp` accounts qualify: never token
accounts (owned by the token program), orders (their rent belongs to the
trader) or any other record. The account keeps exactly its minimum.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Receives the excess lamports.

instructions.name: treasury_lend
docs: Lend part of the treasury. The cUSDC moves to the authority's own account,
which deposits it into the venue in the same transaction, as market
collateral's `deploy_collateral_to_yield` does. It spends the withdrawal
allowance exactly like `admin_withdraw`, so lending can never move money out
of the treasury faster than the policy allows, and it is refused while the
guardian has the treasury frozen.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Must match `global_clp.authority`; owns `lend_account`.

accounts.name: global_vault
docs: Global cUSDC vault, owned by the GlobalClp PDA.

accounts.name: lend_account
docs: The authority's own cUSDC account, which deposits into or withdraws from the
venue in the same transaction.

instructions.name: treasury_recall
docs: Bring lent treasury money back. The authority's account returns `amount`;
`principal` of it repays what was lent at `venue` and the rest is interest.
The returned principal restores the allowance its lend spent, up to the
bucket's burst, so net outflow never exceeds the policy. Allowed while frozen:
money coming home is never blocked.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Must match `global_clp.authority`; owns `lend_account`.

accounts.name: global_vault
docs: Global cUSDC vault, owned by the GlobalClp PDA.

accounts.name: lend_account
docs: The authority's own cUSDC account, which deposits into or withdraws from the
venue in the same transaction.

instructions.name: unfreeze_treasury
docs: Unfreeze treasury withdrawals (guardian only).

instructions.name: update_inventory
docs: Update inventory state (called by keepers after price updates)

accounts.name: authority
docs: Authority/Admin updating inventory state

instructions.name: update_oi
docs: Update OI (open interest) tracking

instructions.name: update_oi_cap
docs: Update OI cap (governance only)

instructions.name: vault_mint_pairs
docs: Use CLP vault USDC to mint L+S pairs via mint-redeem CPI.
The CLP PDA acts as the "user" in the mint_paired CPI, consuming USDC
from the clp_vault and receiving L and S tokens into CLP-owned ATAs.
The resulting tokens are CLP inventory, which the keeper can move into
the native bin-book pools.

accounts.name: global_clp
docs: Global vault — tracks total_deposits and market_allocations

accounts.name: market
docs: mint-redeem Market PDA: must be this CLP's own market, so a vault op
can never mint or redeem against another market's ledger.

accounts.name: clp_vault
docs: CLP vault: the cUSDC source for minting and the payout account for both
redeems. Owned by the CLP PDA and of the market's collateral mint.

accounts.name: market_collateral_vault
docs: Market's collateral vault (destination inside mint-redeem)

accounts.name: long_mint
docs: Long token mint

accounts.name: short_mint
docs: Short token mint

accounts.name: clp_long_account
docs: CLP's long token account: receives minted L, is the L burn source.
Owned by the CLP PDA, so minted inventory can never land in a wallet.

accounts.name: clp_short_account
docs: CLP's short token account: same rules as `clp_long_account`.

accounts.name: dev_token_account
docs: dev_token_account required by mint_paired (must be owned by market.fee_recipient)

accounts.name: oracle
docs: Oracle account (passed through to mint-redeem)

instructions.name: vault_redeem_pairs
docs: Redeem L+S tokens held by the CLP PDA back to USDC (keeper-only, recall path).
Called during withdrawal-driven recall:
vault_redeem_pairs → return_to_global
The CLP PDA signs the CPI to mint-redeem as the "user", burning L+S tokens
from its ATAs and receiving USDC back into clp_vault.

accounts.name: global_clp
docs: Global vault — tracks total_deposits and market_allocations

accounts.name: market
docs: mint-redeem Market PDA: must be this CLP's own market, so a vault op
can never mint or redeem against another market's ledger.

accounts.name: clp_vault
docs: CLP vault: the cUSDC source for minting and the payout account for both
redeems. Owned by the CLP PDA and of the market's collateral mint.

accounts.name: market_collateral_vault
docs: Market's collateral vault (destination inside mint-redeem)

accounts.name: long_mint
docs: Long token mint

accounts.name: short_mint
docs: Short token mint

accounts.name: clp_long_account

instructions.name: vault_redeem_single
docs: Redeem one side (L or S) held by the CLP PDA back to cUSDC at NAV.
Asymmetric counterpart to `vault_redeem_pairs` — used by the keeper's
`pool_depth_balancer` to convert one side's excess deployed inventory
into cUSDC, which can then be re-minted as paired L+S via
`vault_mint_pairs` and redeployed into the thin pool.
Solvency: identical buffer impact as paired redeem. The on-chain
`redeem_single_for_vault` ix enforces a CR ≥ 100% floor post-redeem,
so an underwater vault refuses the operation.
Authority: gated on `clp.authority` via `has_one` (the CLP authority
keypair, not the keeper main wallet) so only the protocol operator
can initiate the cross-side rebalance.

types.name: Clp
docs: Per-market CLP operational account.
Seeds: `[b"clp", market_id]`
After the global vault migration, this account no longer holds LP capital.
It tracks market-specific operational state: inventory risk, yield deployments
and vault pair-minting counters.

docs: Oracle program config account for this market.

docs: Number of active yield deployments

docs: Total amount currently deployed for yield

docs: S tokens currently outstanding from vault minting.

docs: Cumulative USDC used for vault pair minting (informational).

fields.name: retired_venue_state
docs: RETIRED. 136 bytes that once held a fee counter (u64) and four account
addresses (Pubkeys) for a liquidity venue the protocol no longer uses.
Live accounts may still hold that stale data. Nothing reads or writes
these bytes; they keep every later field at its offset. Zero them, or
migrate them, before giving them any new meaning.

fields.name: swap_guards
docs: Swap guards / circuit-breaker config. Default (zeroed) = disabled.

fields.name: swap_window_start
docs: Rolling notional-cap window: start time and cUSDC used so far.

fields.name: swap_prev_price
docs: Last NAV accepted by a swap (for the deviation breaker; 0 = none yet).

fields.name: commit_spread_bps
docs: Keeper-posted committed-order half-spread (bps), driven by the same vol
model as the book. `settle_swap` uses max(this, COMMIT_SPREAD_BPS) so it
never quotes thinner than the 10bps floor. 0 (unset/legacy) → floor.
This is the lever that prices the protocol's short-convexity exposure on
large committed fills (r38: flips a 20x asset from 99% bust → 0%).

docs: Last TWAP update time

docs: Configuration for worst-case quoting

fields.name: oracle_confidence
docs: Oracle confidence interval (updated by keepers)

fields.name: keeper_authority
docs: Whitelisted keeper authority that is allowed to update risk state

fields.name: dev_tax_pct
docs: Dev tax percentage (updated by keeper based on CLP TVL tiers)

fields.name: yield_ceiling_bps
docs: Maximum fraction of total_collateral deployable to yield protocols (basis points).
Default: 6000 (60%). Remaining 40% stays liquid to cover redemptions.

fields.name: deployed_to_yield
docs: Amount of collateral currently deployed to external lending protocols.
Invariant: deployed_to_yield <= total_collateral * yield_ceiling_bps / 10_000

fields.name: total_yield_harvested
docs: Cumulative yield harvested to CLP vault (never decrements, informational).

fields.name: yield_enabled
docs: Whether collateral yield deployment is enabled for this market.

fields.name: buffer_target_bps
docs: Keeper-posted overcollateralization buffer (bps OVER parity), the dynamic
solvency target. Target ratio = 10_000 + buffer_target_bps, clamped to
[MIN_BUFFER_BPS, MAX_BUFFER_BPS]. 0 (legacy/unset) is treated as the default
200 (102%) by `target_ratio_bps()`, so old accounts behave as before until the
keeper posts a value. Sized from σ-regime + live inventory (vol_model::dynamic_buffer).

fields.name: s_gamma_index
docs: Keeper-posted decay scalar on the SHORT NAV, in 1e9 fixed point
(1_000_000_000 = 1.0 = no decay). The effective short NAV is
`(K / l_nav) · s_gamma_index / 1e9`. It only ever ratchets DOWN, by the
realized variance the short pair accrues, so holding the short across a
choppy path costs the decay, which banks as collateral surplus (the
long leg is never touched). `0` (legacy/unset) is read as 1e9 by
`short_gamma_index()`, so old accounts behave exactly as before until
the keeper posts a value. NOT a perp funding rate; there is no periodic
cash transfer; it is a structural mark on the short token's value, so the
1:1 paired round-trip and buy-and-hold mechanics are unchanged at a fixed γ.

fields.name: gamma_day_start_ts
docs: Unix ts the current γ day-bucket opened. 0 = no bucket yet.

fields.name: gamma_day_decay_1e9
docs: γ index units (1e9) decayed inside the current day-bucket. TELEMETRY
ONLY: tracked so an auditor can see the day's total, never enforced.

fields.name: gamma_last_write_ts
docs: Unix ts of the last accepted γ write. Lets an auditor alarm on writer
SILENCE, the failure mode no cap can catch, because it looks like calm.

fields.name: gamma_epoch
docs: Bumped by a re-anchor. Carried in `SetGammaParams` as a CAS so a decay
post computed against a pre-re-anchor γ can never land after the fold
and re-charge the whole epoch.

fields.name: reanchor_count
docs: How many re-anchors this market has seen. 0 = never.

fields.name: genesis_s_price
docs: `initial_s_price` as of genesis, before any re-anchor folded γ into it.
Backfilled lazily on the first re-anchor; 0 = never re-anchored, so the
live `initial_s_price` IS the genesis value.

fields.name: last_reanchor_ts
docs: Unix ts of the last re-anchor. 0 = never.

fields.name: short_payoff_cap_c_1e9
docs: Reserved for the capped short payoff `S = γ·min(K/P, C·K/P₀)` (1e9
fixed). The instruction ships in upgrade #2; the FIELD lands here so
that upgrade is instructions-only and needs no second realloc.
0 = unset = uncapped, i.e. exactly today's behavior.

fields.name: price_adjust_den
docs: Denominator of the cumulative corporate-action ratio. See
`price_adjust_num`. 0 = unset = identity.

fields.name: price_adjust_pending_num
docs: A corporate action ARMED AHEAD of its ex-date: the cumulative pair that
becomes live at `price_adjust_effective_ts`. Until then the current
`price_adjust_num/den` keeps applying.
This exists because arming a ratio early is otherwise actively harmful,
not merely useless. The adjustment multiplies the NEXT raw print, and
before the ex-date that print is still PRE-split, so an early 2:1 would
double the stored price, the 25% move guard would reject every push, and
the market would halt from the moment of arming until the split actually
happened. Gating on a timestamp is what makes "schedule it weeks ahead"
a true statement instead of a longer outage.

fields.name: price_adjust_pending_den
docs: Denominator of the pending pair. See `price_adjust_pending_num`.

fields.name: price_adjust_effective_ts
docs: Unix ts from which the pending pair applies. 0 = nothing pending.
Set it to the ex-date OPEN, the first instant a venue quotes the
post-action price. Misalignment is bounded and self-correcting for
ratios above ~1.333: a print on the wrong side of the boundary is
REJECTED by the 25% guard, not absorbed, so an early or late `ts` costs
rejected pushes rather than a mispriced book. Below ~1.333 nothing
rejects it and the alignment is the only control.

fields.name: price_adjust_last_effective_ts
docs: Most recent activated units boundary, retained after promotion and rescheduling.

types.name: Order
docs: A commit-then-settle order: the user escrowed `amount_in` at `created_at`, and the
keeper's `settle_swap` fills it at the price of an oracle push strictly after that
(price set after the commitment → latency arb impossible → large sizes safe at
NAV ± the committed spread). Settlement is keeper-only (AUDIT CLP-5), so the owner
cannot pick which push fills; any push before `expires_at` qualifies, normally the
first one the keeper sees.
LAYOUT IS LOAD-BEARING for the keeper's getProgramAccounts memcmp filters:
user @ 8 (after discriminator) · market @ 40 · status @ 74
Two sizes exist: `ORDER_LEN_LEGACY` (117, committed before the CLP-5 upgrade, no
recorded accounts) and `ORDER_LEN` (213). Statuses: `ORDER_PENDING` (0) awaits
settle or cancel; `ORDER_CLAIMABLE` (1) holds tokens its owner's recorded account
could not receive, released by the permissionless `claim`. Every other terminal
path CLOSES the account (rent → user), which makes repeated settle attempts
idempotent.

fields.name: user_out
docs: The payout account given at commit. Settle pays only here, or into the
order's claim account when this one cannot receive.

fields.name: user_in
docs: The source account given at commit, where refunds and leftovers go.

fields.name: claim_payer
docs: Who paid the claim account's rent (the settling keeper) and gets it back
at `claim`; default while no claim account exists.

types.name: OrderCapped
docs: A committed order the exposure cap filled only in part; `refunded_in` went
back to the owner with the escrow. `exposure` is traders' net position (E,
cUSDC atoms) before the fill.

types.name: OrderHeld
docs: A settle or cancel could not deliver to the owner's account: `held_in`
stays in the escrow, `held_out` sits in the claim account, and the order is
ORDER_CLAIMABLE until `claim`.

types.name: Pool
docs: v2 native DISCRETE-BIN quote book for ONE synth side (long or short) vs
cUSDC. `asks`/`bids` are per-bin reserves around `base_price_1e6` (≈ side
NAV), priced at `base·r^±k` with `r = 1 + step_bps/1e4`. Swaps walk the bins
(real slippage); the keeper repositions to NAV with a skewed shape via
`set_pool_shape`. See `clmm.rs`.
NAMING: despite the `CLMM_*` env vars and the `clmm.rs` filename, this is
NOT a Uniswap-v3-style concentrated-liquidity AMM. There is no continuous
`x·y=k` curve and no permissionless LPs: each bin holds a fixed reserve at a
fixed price (constant-sum within a bin), and the ladder is POSTED by the
keeper rather than emerging from deposits. It is a discrete-bin liquidity
book (the Trader Joe "Liquidity Book" family), with a single quoter. The
old names are kept for config compatibility; docs say "bin book".

types.name: PoolSwapParams
docs: Args for `pool_swap`, as a single struct so the borsh deserialize is ONE
unit — the v1.45 SBF toolchain miscompiles per-arg field-offset assignment
for multi-scalar-arg instructions (see mint-redeem's InitMarketParams).
Wire format is byte-for-byte identical to the old 3-arg form.

fields.name: losses_absorbed

types.name: RevenueAttribution
docs: Splits protocol revenue into keeper self-flow vs external-user flow.
Seeds: `[b"revenue_attribution"]` — global singleton, initialized once by
the admin AFTER the program upgrade (pool_swap requires it to exist).
`global_clp.total_fees_accumulated` stays untouched as the legacy bucket;
these counters start at zero from `started_at`, so pre-existing revenue is
simply unattributed. A pool_swap's revenue is its spread capture vs
`base_price_1e6` (every ask fill is strictly above base, every bid fill
strictly below — see clmm.rs — so the capture is non-negative), classified
by whether the swap signer is a registered keeper authority. ALL
deposit_profit and liquidity-recall flow is keeper flow by construction
(keeper-attested amounts), regardless of source tag.

fields.name: fees_external
docs: Spread capture (cUSDC atoms) from pool_swap by non-keeper signers.
The ONLY counter that may feed a headline "trading APR".

fields.name: fees_keeper
docs: Spread capture from keeper-signed pool_swap + deposit_profit (net of
dev tax).

fields.name: volume_external
docs: cUSDC notional of non-keeper pool_swap volume (informational).

fields.name: volume_keeper
docs: cUSDC notional of keeper pool_swap volume (informational).

fields.name: deposit_by_source
docs: deposit_profit net amounts by source tag: [arb, recycled_lp_fees,
yield_harvest, other]. Indexed by the PROFIT_SOURCE_* constants.

fields.name: started_at
docs: When attribution began — the honest annualization denominator for
fees_external (protocol inception would understate a young counter).

fields.name: keeper_authorities
docs: Signers classified as keeper flow. Default pubkeys are inert (a
default-key signer can't exist). clp.authority is ALSO treated as
keeper in pool_swap, so this list is for the operational keeper
wallet(s) and test keypairs.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Headroom for future counters WITHOUT realloc (v1.45 realloc landmine).

types.name: RevenueAttributionParams
docs: Args for init/configure of the RevenueAttribution singleton.

fields.name: keeper_authorities
docs: Signers to classify as keeper flow in pool_swap. Default pubkeys are

fields.name: route
docs: 0 = instant CLP, 1 = pool, 2 = committed settlement.

fields.name: reference_price
docs: NAV for CLP routes; the book's base price for pool execution.

fields.name: spread_capture
docs: Execution spread versus reference, NOT withdrawn/realized net revenue.

types.name: SwapGuardsState
docs: v2 native oracle-pegged swap guards (persisted on `Clp`). Mirrors the pure
`swap::SwapGuards` used by the math/breaker logic; `to_guards()` converts.
All-zero default (`enabled=false`) keeps swaps OFF until `configure_swap` is
called — safe for accounts realloc'd into the new layout.

fields.name: enabled
docs: Master on/off for the native swap path.

fields.name: frozen
docs: Hard kill switch (admin or auto-set on oracle degradation).

fields.name: spread_bps
docs: LP edge applied to NAV, bps.

fields.name: max_staleness_secs
docs: Reject if the NAV/TWAP is older than this many seconds.

fields.name: max_confidence_bps
docs: Reject if oracle confidence exceeds this (bps of price).

fields.name: max_deviation_bps
docs: Reject if NAV moved more than this vs the last accepted price (bps).

fields.name: window_cap_usd
docs: Rolling-window notional cap (cUSDC, 6-dec); 0 = uncapped.

fields.name: window_secs
docs: Rolling-window length (seconds).

fields.name: collateral_floor_bps
docs: Minimum collateralization (bps) that must hold AFTER a swap.

types.name: TreasuryLendParams
docs: Args for `treasury_lend` (one struct: the v1.45 multi-arg landmine).

fields.name: venue
docs: `YieldProtocol` discriminant: 0 Kamino, 1 MarginFi, 2 Other, 3 Solend, 4 JupiterLend.

types.name: TreasuryLimitsApplied
docs: Limits took effect: at once (`immediate`, a tightening) or after the delay.

types.name: TreasuryLimitsParams
docs: Args for `set_treasury_limits` (one struct: the v1.45 multi-arg landmine).

types.name: TreasuryLimitsProposed
docs: A loosening change was stored as pending. Alert on this: `loosened` names
the fields that loosen (bits `TreasuryPolicy::LOOSEN_*`: 1 rate up, 2 burst
up, 4 delay shorter, 8 new destination, 16 new guardian), `pending_at` is
when anyone may apply it, and `replaced_pending` is set when it overwrote
an earlier pending change (restarting the clock). The guardian vetoes with
`cancel_treasury_limits`.

types.name: TreasuryPolicy
docs: Treasury withdrawal policy for `admin_withdraw` (singleton PDA, seeds
`[b"treasury_policy"]`). Replaces the AdminWithdrawWindow cap, which was
10% of a `total_deposits` counter that is 0 on devnet (so the cap was 0).
Withdrawals draw on a token bucket: `allowance` accrues at `rate_per_sec`
up to `burst`, and each withdrawal spends it. Funds may only go to
`destination`. A change that tightens every limit applies at once; any
loosening waits `delay_secs` (the delay in force when it was proposed) as
a pending change that the guardian can cancel. The guardian (a separate
key) can also freeze withdrawals, and only the guardian can unfreeze.

fields.name: guardian
docs: Can freeze, unfreeze, cancel pending changes and rotate itself.

fields.name: destination
docs: The only cUSDC token account `admin_withdraw` pays.

fields.name: rate_per_sec
docs: Allowance accrual, collateral atoms per second.

fields.name: burst
docs: Bucket capacity: the most that can ever be withdrawn at once.

fields.name: delay_secs
docs: Delay before a LOOSENING change can be applied, seconds.

fields.name: allowance
docs: Currently withdrawable, as of `last_accrual_at`.

fields.name: pending_at
docs: When the pending change becomes applicable; 0 = no pending change.

types.name: TreasuryPolicyParams
docs: Args for `init_treasury_policy` (one struct: the v1.45 multi-arg landmine).

types.name: TreasuryRecallParams
docs: Args for `treasury_recall`.

fields.name: amount
docs: cUSDC returned to the treasury vault.

fields.name: principal
docs: The part of `amount` that repays principal at `venue`; the rest is interest.

types.name: TreasuryYield
docs: The treasury's lending ledger, seeds `[b"treasury_yield"]`. The cUSDC itself sits
in the authority's venue receipts, the pattern market collateral already uses
(mint-redeem `deploy_collateral_to_yield`); this records what the treasury is
owed at each venue, indexed by `YieldProtocol` discriminant.

fields.name: by_venue
docs: Principal out at each venue: Kamino, MarginFi, Other, Solend, JupiterLend.

fields.name: principal
docs: Sum of `by_venue`.

fields.name: interest
docs: Interest returned to the treasury, all time.

types.name: WorstCaseQuotingConfig
docs: Configuration for worst-case quoting
Protects protocol from informed traders exploiting confidence interval edges

fields.name: enabled
docs: Whether worst-case quoting is enabled

fields.name: normal_confidence_multiplier
docs: Confidence multiplier in Normal state (100 = 1x, 150 = 1.5x)

fields.name: proxy_confidence_multiplier
docs: Confidence multiplier in Proxy state

fields.name: stress_confidence_multiplier
docs: Confidence multiplier in Stress state (also the starting point for Recovery Dutch auction)

types.name: YieldDeployment
docs: Yield deployment to a specific protocol

fields.name: protocol
docs: Protocol where yield is deployed

fields.name: amount_deployed
docs: Amount deployed

fields.name: deployed_at
docs: Timestamp of deployment

fields.name: last_harvest
docs: Last yield harvest time

fields.name: total_yield_earned
docs: Total yield earned from this deployment

fields.name: is_active
docs: Whether this deployment is active

types.name: YieldProtocol
docs: Yield protocol identifier
Tag only — the on-chain CLP program treats every variant identically
(just records the deployment in `yield_deployments[]`). The actual
deposit/withdraw CPI is composed off-chain by the keeper, which means
adding a new venue here does NOT require any further program changes,
only a keeper-side adapter. Append-only for backwards-compat with
existing on-chain `YieldDeployment` records that store the discriminant
byte: never reorder.

types.name: YieldStrategyConfig
docs: Yield strategy configuration

fields.name: normal_deployment_bps
docs: Maximum % of idle collateral to deploy for yield (basis points)
Dynamic based on risk state

fields.name: min_liquid_reserve
docs: Absolute minimum reserve to keep liquid (in USDC, 6 decimals)

fields.name: min_liquid_reserve_bps
docs: Target liquid reserve as a share of TVL

fields.name: oi_liquidity_buffer_bps
docs: Extra reserve linked to live open interest

fields.name: enabled
docs: Whether yield strategy is enabled
